title: Appendix removal
what: A surgeon removes the inflamed appendix, a small pouch of the bowel. Usually through small cuts in the belly, sometimes through one small incision.
why: For acute appendicitis. This is urgent surgery. Without it, the infection can spread through the whole belly.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: When and where the pain started
All your medicines, especially blood thinners
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes

prepare.title: If your belly hurts
prepare.text: Do not eat or drink until a doctor examines you. Do not put heat on your belly.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not take painkillers or laxatives before the exam. They can hide the signs.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood and urine tests, an ultrasound, and sometimes other tests. The hospital does them all.

steps: The surgeon examines your belly, and blood and urine are tested
A thin tube called an IV is put into a vein
In the operating room, the anesthesiologist puts you to sleep
The surgeon removes the appendix through small cuts or an incision
You wake up in the recovery room, then move to a ward
feel: Pain where the cuts or stitches are. You will get pain medicine
Sometimes shoulder pain from gas in the belly. It passes in 1 to 2 days
after: You are usually allowed to get up the same day or the next day
You start eating slowly, when the doctor says so
Do not lift anything heavy for a few weeks
Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own. The surgeon will tell you
red_flags: Before surgery: belly pain getting worse, fever, or vomiting. Call emergency services
After surgery: a fever over 38 degrees, or belly pain getting worse
Redness or pus where the cuts or stitches are

faq.q: How do I know it is appendicitis?
faq.a: You cannot know for sure on your own. Pain often starts near the belly button and moves to the lower right. There may be nausea and fever. With pain like this, call emergency services.

faq.q: Can you live without an appendix?
faq.a: Yes. Your body works normally without it.
